public_rationale: On January 6, 2026, JLL reported average global equipment lead times of 33 weeks, 50% above pre-2020 levels [e1]. Latitude Media reported on February 24, 2026 that 26% of 110 projects expected online in 2025 were delayed into 2026 [e4]. These reports document delays and constraints without isolating understated physical construction time as their cause [e1] [e4]. On March 18, 2025, Crusoe targeted energization of Abilene's first two buildings in the first half of 2025 [e2]. Its September 30, 2025 release reported that construction began in June 2024 and those buildings were energized within a year [e3]. These company disclosures concern one phase's energization and do not establish industry-wide differences between public schedules and actual construction durations [e2] [e3].
limitations: No representative comparison separates construction and commissioning delays from power, permitting, equipment, labor, financing and scope changes.
The evidence does not establish how much public representations understated build durations.
The Abilene disclosures do not provide an exact energization date or establish full-campus operation.
JLL's equipment measure is global. Sightline's underlying project dataset was unavailable for inspection.
The approximately 3 GW figure was not verified as comprehensive US operational IT capacity.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Data center delays are caused not only by power but because building data centers takes far longer than the industry admits.

statement.excerpt: Nevertheless, I also think there’s another more-obvious reason: it takes way longer to build a data center than anybody is letting on, as evidenced by the fact that we only added 3GW or so of actual capacity in America in 2025.
statement.document_title: The AI Industry Is Lying To You

from_speaker: it takes way longer to build a data center
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that physical construction and commissioning take materially longer than industry representations imply, independently contributing to delays alongside power constraints.
Do not interpret 'anybody' as a literal claim that no industry participant ever disclosed a long schedule.
Assess the 2025 experience and construction status through the March 24, 2026 post.
The approximately 3 GW statement is a proposed supporting observation, not sufficient proof of the causal explanation.
Compare the same project phase and milestone; energization, delivery of GPUs and operation are not interchangeable.
criteria.support_condition: Representative project records show material schedule overruns attributable to construction or commissioning constraints beyond power availability, and show that public representations understated those durations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative matched records show build durations broadly consistent with public representations, or establish that the relevant delays arose from other causes rather than understated physical construction time.

evidence.explanation: Long equipment lead times are a plausible constraint beyond obtaining grid power. This global measure does not establish understated US construction schedules or separate electrical equipment from other equipment.
This establishes a specific public target for energizing the first two buildings. It promises neither completion of all eight buildings nor full GPU operation at that milestone.

evidence.excerpt: the first two buildings were energized
evidence.explanation: The release dates construction's start to June 2024 and reports energization within a year, consistent with the earlier first-half-2025 target. This is material counterevidence for the cited example, but one company-reported phase cannot settle an industry-wide causal claim.

evidence.excerpt: struggled to come online on time.
evidence.locator: Olivia Wang quotation discussing projects planned for 2025
evidence.explanation: A Sightline analyst describes missed schedules among the earlier project cohort. The report discusses several possible constraints and does not isolate understated physical construction time as the independent cause.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative project records covering 2025 through March 24, 2026 that compare original public schedules, revisions and actual dates for the same milestones. Documented delay causes must show whether construction and commissioning independently caused material overruns and whether public representations understated those durations.
